mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.3% triggers a risk premium adjustment that elevates S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3% in the current month
failure_condition: Over a 12-month rolling window, 20-day forward returns during inflation spikes are not statistically different from zero (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment momentum as measured by PAYEMS outpaces wage growth (UNRATE), signaling a labor market expansion that boosts equity valuations and drives positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth rate > UNRATE growth rate over the current month
regime_hint: strong labor market with wage moderation
failure_condition: Across 3 consecutive quarters where PAYEMS > UNRATE, 60-day forward returns are negative on average (mean < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in RSAFS industrial production below -2% for two consecutive months predicts a near-term demand softening, which is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls below -2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: During such double-month declines, 5-day forward returns are not statistically different from baseline (t-test p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly acceleration in industrial production (INDPRO) growth above +2% suggests supply-side expansion that outpaces demand, lowering forward discounting costs and producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: During 20-day windows after such acceleration, forward returns are negative in >50% of cases (empirical frequency).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS rises above 4.5% for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 60-day forward return tends to be negative due to higher real borrowing costs and reduced risk appetite.
failure_condition: During such episodes, 60-day forward returns are not systematically negative (mean ≥ 0, p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in UNRATE below 6% combined with a sustained monthly decline in HOUST housing starts (-10% month-over-month) indicates a softening labor market and housing cycle, which precedes negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 6% AND HOUST < prev_month by >10% in the current month
regime_hint: labor market cooling with housing contraction
failure_condition: During such combined signals, 20-day forward returns remain positive in >40% of instances (empirical frequency).

mechanism_narrative: A two-month consecutive decline in GDPC1 personal consumption expenditures (PCE) by at least 1% is interpreted as early-stage demand weakness and predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls by ≥1% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: During such double-month declines, 5-day forward returns are not statistically different from baseline (t-test p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When the interaction between INDPRO and GDPC1 forms a negative cross-correlation at lag +1 month (INDPRO leads GDPC1 by >2%), it signals an imbalance between supply and demand that is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO[t-1] > GDPC1[t-1] + 2% for the current month
failure_condition: During such cross-correlation events, 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (mean ≤ 0, p-value > 0.05).
